subject: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@medixa-health.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Eric Soto <eric.soto@medixa-health.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising. Before we start sending any production traffic for the pilot, our legal and security teams asked for a short confirmation on a few items so we can move to procurement: 

1) Learning exclusion: we need an explicit confirmation in writing that Redwood will not use any prompts, responses, or derived artifacts from Medixa traffic to further train or tune models (including internal research datasets).
2) Prompt/response IP: Medixa needs assurance that prompts and responses remain the customer's data and that no derivative IP is claimed by Redwood.
3) Subprocessors & residency: can you send the current subprocessor list and confirm whether any processing for the pilot will cross borders (we are scoped for US-only processing for now)?
4) Evidence items: if you can provide a short evidence pack (audit log extract, config showing learning disabled, and a manifest of the env/regions) that would help our security review.

We don't expect changes to the existing DPA for the pilot, but legal will likely ask for a short DPA amendment or confirmation email that captures the learning exclusion. Can you point us to the right person on your side to do that quickly?

Appreciate a reply by EOD Monday UTC if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Engineering Security
Medixa Health

Attachment: medixa_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet listing items)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@medixa-health.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes on learning exclusion for the pilot (we can commit not to use Medixa traffic to train or tune models); yes on customer ownership of prompts/responses; we will run processing in US regions only for the pilot. I'll loop in Legal and Ops below with proposed next steps and an evidence bundle.

Laura/laura: can Legal produce a one-paragraph amendment or confirmation for the DPA (language we can send back to Medixa) that explicitly states the learning exclusion and ownership of outputs?

Dev: can Ops produce an export of the deployment configuration showing region bindings, subprocessor list, and a short audit-log extract demonstrating the learning flag is off? If possible include a manifest of artifact retention policies.

Olivia — I'll aim to get a first-cut package Monday morning PST and a signed DPA amendment within a few days.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP

Hi all,

Draft language below is fine as an amendment for a short-term pilot; legal is comfortable with the ask so long as operational controls are verifiable. Suggested paragraph to include: 

"For the duration of the Pilot (as defined in the Statement of Work), Redwood Inference shall not use, incorporate, or otherwise apply Customer prompts, responses, or derived artifacts from Customer traffic for model training, tuning, or research activities. Customer retains all right, title and interest in prompts and responses and any direct derivatives thereof. Redwood's standard DPA and subprocessor disclosures apply; Redwood shall provide an evidence package showing applicable subprocessor processing locations and configuration demonstrating learning is disabled upon Customer request."

A few notes: 
- This is a pilot-limited commitment; if Medixa wants a broader, perpetual restriction we need to talk commercial and legal scope (possible contract amendment).
- Ops evidence should include a signed manifest (csv) and a short extract of audit logs showing the learning flag for the Medixa tenant was set to false before traffic onset.
- We should also provide the current subprocessor list and the specific regions for the dedicated pool we propose for the pilot.

I can produce the redline doc; Karthik / Dev, please confirm the list of subprocessors and the artifact we can attach.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa_amendment_redline.docx (proposed one-paragraph amendment)

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@medixa-health.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP

Hi Olivia and team — ops update and evidence plan: 

1) Subprocessors: current list attached (medixa_data_flow.pdf includes infra diagram). For the pilot we propose isolating processing to our us-west-2 pool (no cross-border routing). Subprocessors: AWS (us-west-2), FastCache Inc. (edge KV caching in us-west-2), LogStream Ltd. (audit log ingestion, US-only).

2) Learning toggles: we will set the tenant-level "model_improvement" flag to false prior to any traffic; that flag disables telemetry capture for model improvement paths and blocks any routing to internal research datasets.

3) Evidence bundle: I'll attach "evidence_export_manifest.csv" with (a) tenant config dump, (b) short audit log snippet with timestamps, and (c) region binding for the Dedicated pool. Expect that to be attached to the DPA amendment email.

4) Retention: prompt/response logs for the pilot are retained for 30 days for debugging and then auto-archived; we can configure shorter retention if Medixa needs.

Next steps: I will produce the csv and a sanitized audit extract by EOD. Laura, once you sign off on the DPA paragraph we can push the amendment to Medixa and attach evidence.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: medixa_data_flow.pdf (diagram), evidence_export_manifest.csv (manifest stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@medixa-health.com>, Eric Soto <eric.soto@medixa-health.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medixa pilot: confirmation on learning exclusion and prompt/response IP

Olivia / Eric — thanks for the patience and the clear asks. Attached is the short DPA amendment (redline + clean) and an evidence bundle we prepared for the pilot. Summary: 

- Commitment: Redwood will not use Medixa prompts or responses to train or tune models for the duration of the Pilot (see attached amendment language).
- Ownership: Medixa retains prompts/responses and direct derivatives. Redwood does not assert derivative model ownership.
- Subprocessors & Residency: Processing for the pilot is confined to the us-west-2 dedicated pool; subprocessors are listed in medixa_data_flow.pdf.
- Evidence: evidence_export_manifest.csv contains tenant_config, an audit log extract showing model_improvement=false at 2026-07-13T11:00:02Z, and region binding details.
- Retention: default 30-day debug retention; we can reduce to 7 days by configuration if you need.

Next steps for Medixa: 1) Review the attached amendment language, 2) confirm acceptance via reply or countersign DocuSign link, 3) let Ops know if you want retention shortened prior to onboarding.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the evidence items.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_amendment_redline.docx, medixa_data_flow.pdf, evidence_export_manifest.csv
